blocks.text: 你觉得这桩合并有多大说服力，大概取决于你在多大程度上相信埃隆·马斯克关于想去火星、或者说“传播意识之光”的说法——他在本周的 SpaceX 财报电话会（以及更早的 S-1）上就是这么说的。如今，一个有一定常识的人都知道，我们并没有技术支持人类在太空生存——坦白说，甚至连构建这项技术的原始信息都没有。所以这意味着要靠机器人。但地球与月球或火星之间的延迟导致控制机器人很困难。因此，拥有能够在极少地球监督下自主决策的人工智能机器人，就是科幻逻辑的下一步。

blocks.text: 如果你相信马斯克的故事，我们谈论的技术正通过自动驾驶汽车（Tesla）、LLM（SpaceX）和人形机器人（Tesla）来开发，而所有这些都需要数据中心（SpaceX）。方便的是，我们刚好看过这两家公司的财报。另一方面，如果你把火星视为马斯克用来解释其公开行为的有用虚构，那么，马斯克从这桩合并中能获得大量金钱和大量控制权。

blocks.text: 马斯克在最近的 SpaceX 财报电话会上表示，SpaceX 与 Tesla“合并有很多好处”。为什么？“在开发超级智能软件方面合作，能收获很多。”但人工智能——啊，抱歉，是超级智能软件并不是 SpaceX 目前真正从事的业务。在周二的第三季度财报中，SpaceX 报告称人工智能——抱歉抱歉，是超级智能部门实现 75.6 亿美元营收。子类别“SI 解决方案与基础设施营收”——我认为这是把 Grok、Cursor 和新云业务打包在一起——跃升至 70 亿美元，是上一季度的三倍多。其中一部分来自并入 Cursor，后者贡献了 6.08 亿美元营收。DA Davidson 分析师 Gil Luria 表示，这 70 亿美元中的其余大部分很可能是向 Anthropic 和 Google 出租算力；Grok 的贡献可能较小。

inlines.text: Macroharder

blocks.text: SpaceX 和特斯拉之间已有一些合作；例如，SpaceX 购买了价值 1.31 亿美元的滞销 Cybertruck。它过去还持有过特斯拉债券。更关键的是，两家公司还共同宣布了两个 AI——算了，我们就沿用 AI 这个说法——项目：Terafab 和 Macrohard。

inlines.text: SpaceX 和特斯拉之间已有一些合作；例如，SpaceX

blocks.text: Terafab 是马斯克打算在得克萨斯州建造并运营、为自己供应芯片的芯片制造项目；英特尔与马斯克算是合作伙伴，共同开发这项技术。Macrohard 则是一个 AI 项目，让人们模拟微软已经做出来的软件。至少我认为它应该是这个意思。打出后一个名字让我祈祷小行星现在就撞上我们所有人，所以也许幸运的是，自 3 月宣布以来我们没怎么听到它的消息。

blocks.text: 假设你在体质上与我截然不同，而且富有得多，因此你持有一些特斯拉的股票。你显然是埃隆·马斯克的忠实信徒——但你也注意到，这个人的注意力持续时间就像一只吸了可卡因的松鼠。他基本上时刻都在X上，而且常常带着种族主义色彩。他不断出现在白宫，做些惹恼潜在特斯拉客户的事情。然后他又公开与总统交恶。有时他对火箭兴致勃勃，有时又对狗狗币兴致勃勃，有时又特别痴迷于Grok，有时又会想想汽车的事。但你注意到，不管怎样，他最近对汽车的关注少了很多。

blocks.text: 既然他似乎专注于——如果可以说他专注的话——AI，你就会注意到一些相当严重的利益冲突。马斯克旗下的公司“都需要同样稀缺的英伟达芯片来驱动它们的AI，比如”，Matt Levine指出，他是一位长期观察马斯克的人。但如果你把这些公司合并起来，那么，也许你就能打造出最好的通用AI。然后呢？“如果你打造出最好的通用AI模型，也许它就能驾驶汽车、操作机器人、上传人们的大脑，并在Twitter上提供右翼观点。”

blocks.text: 此外，一场大规模的AI基础设施建设正在发生，所以基本上你只要说一句“英伟达”，就会有人给你一大笔钱。合并把所有AI项目归到一处，另外大概还有一些汽车、火箭和卫星。Levine写道：“‘给我们1000亿美元在太空建数据中心，但如果出于某种原因我们没能在太空建数据中心，你可以收回我们在地球上的汽车工厂和数据中心’——这对信贷投资者来说是个不错的说辞。”

inlines.text: 从这个角度看，
显然
SpaceX和特斯拉应该合并，Levine写道：

blocks.text: 它们竟然是两家独立的公司，这太疯狂了！一个人经营着两家庞大的实体AI公司，而且业务高度重叠！这是多么可怕的利益冲突和繁文缛节噩梦！干脆把它们合并，这样这一个人每天来上班时只需一个简单的使命：做出能为这个庞大AI综合体、以及该综合体股东最大化整体价值的选择。如果某些芯片或工程师或钻机或别的什么应该去做机器人，那就去做机器人；如果它们应该去做数据中心，那就去做数据中心。股东们已经走到这一步了；他们当然信任马斯克来做这些决定。只不过现在，做机器人对特斯拉有利、对SpaceX不利；做数据中心对特斯拉不利、对SpaceX有利。马斯克无法同时把两者的利益放在首位。有个简单的解决办法。
当然，事情并没有那么简单。交易的细节至关重要；许多人假设这是一次换股合并。（“我假设收购方会是 SpaceX，部分原因是它的市值更大，但主要是因为马斯克在那里拥有更大的控制权，”Levine 写道。）监管环境也是如此。SpaceX 和特斯拉应该因 AI 而合并的理由，某种程度上不也正是它们不该合并的反垄断理由吗？

inlines.text: 当然，事情并没有那么简单。交易的细节至关重要；许多人假设这是一次换股合并。（“我假设收购方会是 SpaceX，部分原因是它的市值更大，但主要是因为马斯克在那里拥有更大的控制权，”Levine 写道。）监管环境也是如此。SpaceX 和特斯拉应该因 AI 而合并的理由，某种程度上不也正是它们不该合并的反垄断理由吗？

blocks.text: 当前的监管环境，在很大程度上要归因于马斯克通过他的 DOGE 亲信们的干预，姑且说是宽松的。现任总统唐纳德·特朗普的任期还剩两年。此外，市场已开始对 AI 出现一波又一波的紧张情绪。今年夏天早些时候，出现了Situational Awareness 事件，随后又有更近期的 CoreWeave 事件，嗯，投资者情绪可能正在转变。这意味着“有一股推动力要在 2027 年上半年宣布交易，以便在本届政府任内完成交割，”Bloomberg 写道，并将此归因于“知情人士”。

blocks.text: 马斯克从这次合并中得到什么？嗯，控制权，这是他历来最钟爱的东西。根据 Bloomberg 的报道，这次合并还可能为他的净资产增加 1100 亿美元。然而更有趣的是，这次合并与马斯克巨额特斯拉薪酬方案之间的相互作用。如果发生法律上的控制权变更——例如，因为 SpaceX 收购了特斯拉——马斯克巨额薪酬方案中的运营里程碑就会失效。

blocks.text: The degree to which you find this merger compelling likely has to do with the degree to which you believe Elon Musk about wanting to go to Mars, or “spread the light of consciousness,” as he put it in this week’s SpaceX earnings call (and earlier S-1). Now, a reasonably informed person knows that we don’t have the technology — or, frankly, even the raw information to build the technology — in order to support human life in space. So that means robots. But a lag between Earth and the Moon or Mars makes for difficulty in controlling the robots. So having artificially intelligent robots who can make decisions on their own with minimal supervision from Earth is the next sci-fi logic step.

blocks.text: Musk said on the recent SpaceX earnings call that “there’s a lot of merit to combining” SpaceX and Tesla. Why? “There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software.” But artificial intelligence — ah, excuse me, super intelligence software isn’t the business SpaceX is really in right now. In its Q3 earnings on Tuesday, SpaceX reported $7.56 billion in revenue from the artificial intelligence — sorry, sorry, super intelligence division. The subcategory “SI solutions & infrastructure revenues” — which I think is Grok, Cursor, and the neocloud business wrapped together — jumped to $7 billion, or more than three times what it was last quarter. Now some of this was getting Cursor stapled on, which added $608 million in revenue. Most of the rest of that $7 billion was likely renting out compute to Anthropic and Google; Grok is probably contributing less, says Gil Luria, an analyst at DA Davidson.

blocks.text: Let’s say you are constitutionally very different from me, and much richer, and for this reason you own a number of shares in Tesla. You’re a big believer in Elon Musk — obviously — but you notice that the man has an attention span of a squirrel on cocaine. He’s on X basically constantly and often racistly. He keeps showing up at the White House to do stuff that pisses off would-be Tesla customers. Then he publicly feuds with the president. Sometimes he’s very excited about rockets, and sometimes he’s very excited about Dogecoin and sometimes he’s really into Grok and sometimes he thinks about cars. But you notice that one way or the other he’s been thinking about cars a lot less lately.

blocks.text: Since he seems to be focused — insofar as he can be said to focus — on AI, you notice some pretty big conflicts of interest. Musk’s companies “all need the same scarce Nvidia chips to power their AI, for instance,” notes Matt Levine, a longtime Musk observer. But if you combine the companies, well, maybe you build the best general-purpose AI. And then? “If you build the best general-purpose AI model, maybe it can drive the cars and operate the robots and upload people’s brains and serve right-wing takes on Twitter.”

blocks.text: It’s crazy that they are separate companies! One guy runs two gigantic physical AI companies with huge overlaps! What a nightmare of conflicts of interest and red tape! Just merge them, so that the one guy can come into the office each day with a simple mandate: Make the choices that maximize overall value for the giant AI complex, and for the shareholders of that complex. If some chips or engineers or drills or whatever should be working on robots, work on the robots; if they should be working on data centers, work on the data centers. The shareholders have come this far; surely they trust Musk to make those decisions. It’s just that right now, working on the robots is good for Tesla and bad for SpaceX; working on the data centers is bad for Tesla and good for SpaceX. Musk can’t put both of their interests first. There’s an easy fix.

It’s not exactly that simple, of course. The details of the deal matter; a lot of people are assuming a stock-for-stock merger. (“I assume the acquirer would be SpaceX, in part because it has a bigger market capitalization but mostly because of Musk’s greater control there,” Levine writes.) So does the regulatory environment. The case that SpaceX and Tesla should combine due to AI is also kind of an antitrust reason they shouldn’t?

blocks.text: The current regulatory environment is, in large part due to Musk’s meddling via his DOGE cronies, let’s say lax. Donald Trump, the current president, has two more years left in his term. Also, the markets have started getting waves of nervousness around AI. Earlier this summer, there was the Situational Awareness thing, and then there was the more recent CoreWeave thing, and, well, investor sentiment may be changing. That means “there’s a push to announce a deal by the first half of 2027 so that it closes during this administration,” Bloomberg writes, attributing this to “people who are familiar with the matter.”

blocks.text: Shares and shares alike

inlines.text: Shares and shares alike

blocks.text: Musk has more control at SpaceX than he does at Tesla. His voting power is above 50 percent, because he owns special supervoting shares. He is the CEO, CTO, and chairman of the board. Shareholders are very limited in how they can legally challenge that power. The filing puts it this way: “This will limit or preclude your ability to influence corporate matters and the election of our directors.”

Shareholders are very limited in how they can legally challenge that power. The filing puts it this way: “This will limit or preclude your ability to influence corporate matters and the election of our directors.”

blocks.text: At Tesla, however, Musk only has about 20 percent of the vote. (“Only!”) So in a stock-for-stock merger, where SpaceX is the acquirer, Musk suddenly has voting control of the whole enchilada. “He gets voting control of Tesla in the only way he can,” says Ann Lipton, a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder’s law school. “He can’t change it to a dual-class entity now that it’s publicly traded. This is the only way to do it.”

blocks.text: Both companies are based in Texas, which makes it very difficult for shareholders to sue, says Lipton. “The chances of a shareholder being able to sue on the Tesla or SpaceX side are vanishingly small because Texas has erected so many barriers to shareholder litigation.” So there’s that risk gone.

blocks.text: Leave aside the more complicated issues of national security (for SpaceX) and antitrust. At a federal level, securities laws are largely “Did you disclose it?” notes Lipton. So the SEC, or what remains of it, will want to see that everything is disclosed to shareholders before the vote. As long as the disclosures are accurate, that’s that. At the state level, there may be some issues — it’s a breach of fiduciary duty to create an unfair transaction as a result of conflicts of interest — but Shari Redstone did merge Paramount and CBS, so it’s not impossible.

blocks.text: What does Musk get from this merger? Well, control, a thing he historically loves most of all. Potentially also, the combination adds $110 billion to his net worth, according to Bloomberg. More interesting, however, is how the merger interacts with Musk’s massive Tesla compensation package. If there’s a legal change of control — for instance, because SpaceX buys Tesla — the operational milestones in Musk’s enormous pay package fall away.

blocks.text: What matters then is Tesla’s valuation. If SpaceX pays $2 trillion or more, Musk gets a payout. At $2 trillion, Musk gets $6 billion of shares. He also gets accelerated vesting of shares from his 2018 pay package — which would otherwise have vested in 2028. The change of control also means he can sell them sooner.

blocks.text: Is that good for SpaceX? Assuming we wind up at or around the $2 trillion figure, we’re looking at basically a merger of equals — which means current SpaceX shareholders get diluted all to hell. Worse, Tesla’s business is stagnating, and its AI ambitions are expensive. “It’s likely that SpaceX and Tesla combined will spend close to a staggering $50 billion on capex in Q4, and their businesses won’t come close to covering that number,” writes Shawn Tully in Fortune.

blocks.text: So on a numbers basis, I kind of think no, not really, not that good for SpaceX. But none of Musk’s businesses are about numbers in the end — they are, to some extent, about how much you believe in Elon Musk. That’s what the Tesla valuation versus regular automakers was about in the first place. So sure, fine, slap them together and see what happens. The people who are buying what Musk’s selling, at this point, surely know what they signed up for.
